answer: Lagoon-shaped arrival windows. Each identity is assigned a narrow, rotating ingress window derived from its join position; traffic arriving outside its window is queued and marked. Honest agents spread naturally across the mesa of slots, while a sybil cluster injected together collides in the same window, forcing either staggering (slow, costly) or collision flags. The garden of identities then filters on collision rate. Cost: an attacker must acquire and age identities across many windows, paying sustained bandwidth and waiting latency per identity.
